response: In a rural adult West African population, resting heart rate (RHR) is indeed relevant when it comes to cardiovascular risk. Significant associations have been observed between RHR and several established cardiovascular risk factors. This suggests that RHR could be a valuable tool in assessing cardiovascular risk in this population. However, prospective studies are needed in sub-Saharan African populations to further establish the potential value of RHR in cardiovascular risk assessment and to determine its usefulness as a predictive factor. By considering RHR alongside other established risk factors, healthcare professionals may be able to better identify and manage cardiovascular risk in rural adult West African populations.
